title: A henselian colimit of pointed etale neighbourhoods is the henselization
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $\mathfrak p\subset A$ a prime ideal with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(A_a)_{a\in I}$ a directed system of $A$-algebras with colimit $H$ and colimit maps $\lambda_a:A_a\to H$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Assume that each $\operatorname{Spec}A_a\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is separated etale of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], that $H$ is a henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_H=\mathfrak pH$, and that for every $a$ the prime $\mathfrak p_a=\lambda_a^{-1}(\mathfrak m_H)$ lies over $\mathfrak p$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p_a)$ is an isomorphism. Then: (1) the induced map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to H$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is local and makes $H$ a henselization of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]; (2) for every $a$, the map $(A_a)_{\mathfrak p_a}\to H$ induced by $\lambda_a$ is local and makes $H$ a henselization of $(A_a)_{\mathfrak p_a}$; (3) for every $a$ and every $n\geq1$ the induced maps $A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak p^nA_{\mathfrak p}\to(A_a)_{\mathfrak p_a}/\mathfrak p_a^n(A_a)_{\mathfrak p_a}\to H/\mathfrak m_H^n$ are ring isomorphisms; hence $A_{\mathfrak p}$, $(A_a)_{\mathfrak p_a}$ and $H$ have canonically isomorphic maximal-ideal completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], compatibly with the maps between these rings. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 08HT (lemma-uniqueness-henselian), with Lemmas 04GN (lemma-henselization) and 04GV (lemma-henselization-different): a henselian local filtered colimit of etale algebras with the given residue field is the henselization; used for ILO V 2.2.7 and 3.2.4, pp.65--68, where the henselized cylinder is written as a filtered colimit of finite type algebras.

proof.text: Put $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$, $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and $k_H=H/\mathfrak m_H$. Since the inverse image of $\mathfrak m_H$ in $A$ is $\mathfrak p$, every element of $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ maps to a unit of $H$. Thus the localization property [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] gives a unique local map $\eta:R\to H$ and an injective field map $k\to k_H$. This field map is surjective: given $x\in H$, [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise](2) writes $x=\lambda_a(b)$. Its residue in $k_H$ is the image of the residue of $b$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak p_a)$, and the latter field is the image of $k$ by hypothesis. Every element of $k_H$ has such a representative $x$, so $k\xrightarrow{\sim}k_H$, with precisely the structural residue map.

source.place: Tags 08HR (lemma-map-into-henselian-colimit), 04GN (lemma-henselization), properties (3)--(4); filtered-colimit representatives as in Tag 00D6.

proof.text: Let $T$ be any henselian local ring and $g:R\to T$ a local map. The inverse image of $\mathfrak m_T$ in $A$ is $\mathfrak p$. Via Step 1, $g$ gives a $k$-algebra map $\tau:k_H\to T/\mathfrak m_T$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] with base ring $A$, source algebra $H=\varinjlim_a A_a$, prime $\mathfrak m_H$, and target $T$. The directed set is nonempty and hence filtered, every stage is etale over $A$, and $\mathfrak m_H$ lies over $\mathfrak p$. We obtain a unique $A$-algebra map $h:H\to T$ with inverse image of $\mathfrak m_T$ equal to $\mathfrak m_H$ and residue map $\tau$. Thus $h$ is local and $h\eta=g$ by uniqueness of localization. Conversely, every local $h$ with $h\eta=g$ induces $\tau$, since $k\to k_H$ is an isomorphism, and hence is the same map by the cited theorem. As $H$ is henselian by hypothesis, this is exactly the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. This proves (1).

source.place: Tag 08HR (lemma-map-into-henselian-colimit); Tag 08HT (lemma-uniqueness-henselian) and the paragraph following Definition 04GQ.

proof.text: Fix $a$, and put $B=(A_a)_{\mathfrak p_a}$ and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak p_aB$. The composite $A\to A_a\to H$ has inverse image $\mathfrak p_a$ of $\mathfrak m_H$ at the middle ring. Thus localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] gives a local map $\beta:B\to H$. The map $R\to B$ is local because $\mathfrak p_a$ lies over $\mathfrak p$, and its residue map is the assumed isomorphism $k\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa(\mathfrak p_a)$. Also $\mathfrak nH=\mathfrak m_H$: one inclusion follows from locality of $\beta$, while the other follows from $\mathfrak pH=\mathfrak m_H$ and $\mathfrak pB\subseteq\mathfrak n$. In particular the residue map of $\beta$ is an isomorphism by Step 1.

source.place: Tag 04GV (lemma-henselization-different), the local maps to the pointed colimit; localization and extension of the indicated ideals.

proof.text: Let $T$ be henselian local and let $g:B\to T$ be local. The composite $R\to B\to T$ is local. Part (1) gives a unique local $h:H\to T$ extending that composite. Compare the two $A$-algebra maps $A_a\to H\xrightarrow{h}T$ and $A_a\to B\xrightarrow{g}T$. Their inverse images of $\mathfrak m_T$ are $\mathfrak p_a$. Their induced maps $\kappa(\mathfrak p_a)\to T/\mathfrak m_T$ coincide, since they agree on $k$ and $k\to\kappa(\mathfrak p_a)$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] to the single etale $A$-algebra $A_a$ and this prime and residue map. Its uniqueness gives equality on $A_a$, hence $h\beta=g$ on $B$ by localization. Any other local extension of $g$ agrees on $R$ and is therefore equal to $h$ by (1). Together with the assumed henselianity of $H$, this verifies [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime] for $B$ and proves (2).

source.place: Tag 08HQ (lemma-map-into-henselian), the single-algebra case of 08HR; Tag 04GV (lemma-henselization-different).

proof.text: Fix $n\geq1$. Use the notation $C=R$ or $C=B$, write $\mathfrak r$ for its maximal ideal, and $u:C\to H$ for $\eta$ or $\beta$ respectively. By Steps 1--4, $u$ has the henselization universal property, induces an isomorphism of residue fields, and $\mathfrak rH=\mathfrak m_H$. Put $C_n=C/\mathfrak r^n$ and $H_n=H/\mathfrak m_H^n$. These are local rings, with local quotient maps and maximal ideals $\mathfrak r/\mathfrak r^n$ and $\mathfrak m_H/\mathfrak m_H^n$, by [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure]. Both maximal ideals have zero $n$th power. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-of-nil-maximal-ideal] makes $C_n$ and $H_n$ henselian, even when the original rings are not Noetherian. The induced map $u_n:C_n\to H_n$ is local, since its residue map is the residue isomorphism of $u$.

source.place: Tag 06RS (lemma-local-dimension-zero-henselian), applied to nilpotent maximal ideals; quotient local structure from Section 07BH.

proof.text: Apply the universal property from (1) or (2), as recorded in [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime], to the local quotient map $q_C:C\to C_n$, whose target is henselian by Step 5. It gives a unique local $v:H\to C_n$ with $vu=q_C$. Locality implies $v(\mathfrak m_H)\subseteq\mathfrak r/\mathfrak r^n$, so $v$ kills $\mathfrak m_H^n$. It therefore factors uniquely as $v=v_nq_H$ for a local map $v_n:H_n\to C_n$, where $q_H:H\to H_n$ is the quotient. For each $c\in C$, $v_nu_n(q_C(c))=v(u(c))=q_C(c)$. Surjectivity of $q_C$ gives $v_nu_n=\mathrm{id}_{C_n}$.

source.place: Tags 08HR and 08HT, universal-property argument applied to the henselian local nilpotent quotient of Step 5.

proof.text: The two maps $u_nv$ and $q_H$ from $H$ to $H_n$ are local and agree after $u:C\to H$, since $u_nvu=u_nq_C=q_Hu$. The target $H_n$ is henselian by Step 5. Uniqueness in the henselization property [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime], proved in (1) and (2), yields $u_nv=q_H$. Substitute $v=v_nq_H$ and use surjectivity of $q_H$ to obtain $u_nv_n=\mathrm{id}_{H_n}$. Thus $u_n$ is a ring isomorphism with inverse $v_n$. Applying this with $C=R$ and $C=B$ proves that both $R/\mathfrak p^nR\to H_n$ and $B/\mathfrak p_a^nB\to H_n$ are the specified canonical isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 08HR and 08HT, uniqueness applied twice to the nilpotent quotients; no Noetherian condition enters.

proof.text: Let $\alpha_n:R/\mathfrak p^nR\to B/\mathfrak p_a^nB$ and $\beta_n:B/\mathfrak p_a^nB\to H_n$ be the induced maps in (3). Their composite is the canonical map $\eta_n:R/\mathfrak p^nR\to H_n$. Step 7 says both $\beta_n$ and $\eta_n$ are isomorphisms, so $\alpha_n=\beta_n^{-1}\eta_n$ is an isomorphism. The ideal equalities $(\mathfrak pR)^n=\mathfrak p^nR$ and $(\mathfrak p_aB)^n=\mathfrak p_a^nB$ follow by multiplying the generators of the extended ideals. This proves all finite-quotient assertions in (3).

source.place: Elementary composition of the canonical quotient maps from Step 7; powers of extended ideals.

proof.text: For $m\geq n$, reduction of $u_m(c\bmod\mathfrak r^m)$ to level $n$ is $u(c)\bmod\mathfrak m_H^n$, equal to $u_n(c\bmod\mathfrak r^n)$. Surjectivity of the quotient maps shows that all reduction squares commute. Their inverses commute as well by composing each square with the inverse isomorphisms. By [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], send a compatible sequence $(c_n)_n$ to $(u_n(c_n))_n$, with inverse $(h_n)_n\mapsto(u_n^{-1}(h_n))_n$. These are mutually inverse ring maps, since operations are componentwise. This constructs $\widehat R\cong\widehat H$ and $\widehat B\cong\widehat H$, and hence $\widehat R\cong\widehat B$, commuting with the completion maps and with $R\to B\to H$. If level $n=0$ is included, all its quotient rings are the zero ring and add no condition.

source.place: Completion as the inverse limit of the quotient rings, Section 00M9; componentwise passage from Step 8.

There are no new nodes and the statement is unchanged. Sources checked in algebra.tex: 08HQ (l.42601) and 08HR (l.42881) match lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit, including the single-étale case; 08HT, 04GN and 04GV give the claim. The proof gets the universal property from 08HR and assumes no cofinality. Step 1: by 00D6(2) every element of H comes from a stage, so k is isomorphic to H/m_H. Step 2: 08HR applies to H with prime m_H. Uniqueness holds because any local h with hη=g has preimage m_H and residue map τ. Step 4: B-linearity comes from 08HQ on the single étale algebra A_a. I checked that both maps A_a→T are A-algebra maps with prime preimage p_a and the same residue map on κ(p_a)≅k. Steps 5–7: C/r^n and H/m_H^n are henselian by 06RS (nil maximal ideal, n≥1, no Noetherian hypothesis), and the inverses come from the universal property with both identities checked. Steps 8–9 (quotients, completions) are elementary. Edge cases: field base; Z at (0) with colimit Q; non-maximal p; stages with extra primes. The hypothesis m_H=pH is redundant but harmless. No cycle: the closure of all 7 proof_deps avoids the item. No duplicates: the strict-henselization and pair-henselization nodes have different hypotheses and conclusions. The parent marked-cylinder node uses clause (1) in Step 12 and clause (3) in Step 13, and the statement supports both. I accept the three generic sec-proper-base-change ring tools as tool_uses.
